documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M establishing care. Has not had a regular doctor since his teens. No specific complaint today; came in because his partner wanted him to "get checked out."

PMH: no chronic medical illness he knows of. Gets headaches a few times a week, usually the morning after drinking, and takes a regular-strength aspirin (325) most days on his own for those and "so the hangover isn't as bad." No GI symptoms.
PSH: none.
Meds: aspirin 325 mg OTC daily. No Rx meds.
Allergies: NKDA.

Substance use, in his words fairly matter-of-fact:
- Cigarettes since about 18, a pack a day, roughly 3 yrs. No quit attempts.
- Alcohol: drinks every day; most nights of the week (5 or 6) it turns into a binge, which he puts at 10-15 drinks. Denies withdrawal shakes or seizures. Doesn't see the drinking as a problem.
- Cocaine: intranasal, mostly on weekends with friends, for a couple of years. No injection use, no other drugs.
AUDIT-C 11.

FH: father has alcohol use disorder and has been incarcerated several times. Mother treated for major depression and generalized anxiety. Older brother with opioid use disorder.
SH: lives with his partner. Picks up construction labor when it's available, otherwise out of work. MassHealth.

ROS otherwise negative. PHQ-9 2.

Exam: Well-appearing young man, relaxed, somewhat guarded about details. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal, no scleral icterus. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly. Skin: several tattoos on forearms. No tremor. Neuro grossly nonfocal.

A/P
1. Severe alcohol use disorder. Long talk about amount and pattern; he is not interested in cutting down at this point and declines a referral to treatment. Gave written info and our number. Will keep asking.
2. Cocaine use disorder. Same conversation; declines.
3. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes. Advised to quit; precontemplative.
4. Headaches, using daily aspirin. Advised it isn't a great habit with this much alcohol (stomach), would rather he cut the drinking. He'll "think about it."
5. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, one-time HCV and HIV screens today. Tdap given (no record of one since childhood).

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, your blood work from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver numbers normal, blood counts normal, cholesterol fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were both negative. Nothing to do on these. The bigger health issue for you is still the drinking and smoking, and my door is open whenever you want to talk about it. See you in a few months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video check-in; we reached out after the missed January appointment. He's at his apartment, identity verified by DOB.

No construction work since March with everything shut down. Says he's "bored mostly." Drinking is the same or a little more, hard to pin down; AUDIT-C 12. Still a pack a day. Cocaine "not much lately," which he puts down to not seeing friends. No chest pain, no breathing trouble, no GI bleeding, no fevers. Still uses aspirin for headaches.

No distress on camera, speech normal, conversational.

A/P: Alcohol, cocaine and tobacco use disorders, unchanged. Not ready to change any of it; declines counseling referral again. Reviewed signs of withdrawal that should send him to the ED if he ever stops abruptly. Asked him to come in for a physical in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24M for a physical; first time in the office since 2019 (one missed visit, one video visit in between).

Interval: no illnesses, no ED visits. Got both Pfizer shots at a pharmacy this spring (April and May, he showed the card). Working again on and off, framing and demo crews.

Habits: still about a pack a day, now ~5 years. Drinking daily with binges most nights; AUDIT-C 11. Cocaine "sometimes, weekends." Aspirin most mornings. No hematemesis, melena, abdominal pain. No withdrawal symptoms.
PHQ-9 1.

Exam: Healthy-appearing. Vitals as recorded. Eyes and oropharynx normal. No lymphadenopathy. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge not felt. Extremities normal. Skin with tattoos, no spider angiomata. No tremor.

A/P
- Severe alcohol use disorder / cocaine use disorder: discussed again in plain terms. He listens politely and says he has it handled. Offered referral to outpatient substance use treatment; declined.
- Nicotine dependence: advised to quit. Not interested.
- Labs today: CMP and CBC.
- Flu shot given. COVID series entered from his card.
RTC 1 yr, sooner if he's ready to work on any of this.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jacob, labs from Wednesday look good. Liver tests, kidneys, electrolytes and blood counts are all in the normal range. No changes needed.

AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit date: 11/23/2022, arrival 01:50, by police
Patient: Jacob Healey, 25 M
Allergies: NKDA
Home meds: aspirin 325 mg daily (OTC)

CC: Medical clearance; police report pt was apprehended breaking into a parked car.

HPI: 25 yo M with heavy alcohol, cocaine and tobacco use brought in by police for medical evaluation. Pt calm and talkative. Asked about the incident he says the only thing he feels bad about is that he got caught; no expression of regret toward the car owner. Mother arrived during the visit and gave collateral: he was suspended from school repeatedly before age 15 for fighting with other students and for stealing from his teachers. By his own account and per police, prior arrests for theft, assault and drug charges. Denies SI/HI. Denies injury tonight.

Social: cigarettes 1 ppd, ~6 yrs. Daily alcohol with binges most nights, 10-15 drinks. Cocaine, intranasal. Intermittent construction work, currently not working.
Family: father with alcohol use disorder, multiple incarcerations; mother with depression and anxiety; brother with opioid use disorder.

Exam: VS within normal range (see flowsheet). Alert, oriented x3, not ataxic, speech clear. Affect flat and indifferent; shows no concern for others affected. Multiple tattoos with violent imagery on arms and chest. Old scars across the knuckles of both hands. No acute injuries. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft.

Labs: blood alcohol 80 mg/dL (0.08%). Urine drug screen positive for cocaine.

Behavioral health evaluation (ED behavioral health clinician): longstanding pattern since childhood of rule-breaking, aggression, theft and disregard for others, persisting into adulthood with arrests; lack of remorse on interview. No psychosis, no mood episode, no acute danger to self or others. Impression: antisocial personality disorder. Co-occurring severe alcohol use disorder and cocaine use disorder. Resources for substance use treatment provided; pt not interested.

ED course: observed, no intervention needed. Medically cleared.
Diagnoses: antisocial personality disorder; alcohol use; cocaine use.
Disposition: discharged 07:30.

[Faxed to PCP office 03/06/2023 in response to records request]

AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, ED visit summary to PCP
Date of service: 07/31/2023 22:40 to 08/01/2023 05:15
Patient: Jacob Healey, 25 M. Allergies: NKDA. Meds: aspirin 325 mg daily OTC.

Chief complaint: intoxication; brought in by partner.

HPI: Second visit here this year (previously 11/2022, brought by police). Partner found him at home drunk this evening and was worried because he has a job interview first thing tomorrow. Pt states he finished a full bottle of whiskey over the evening. Explains he wanted to calm his nerves ahead of the interview, that plenty of people drink and he isn't harming anybody, that drinking makes it easier for him to be around people, and that the pressure of looking for work earns him a night off now and then. Does not think his drinking is a problem and believes he could stop if he decided to. No other ingestion reported tonight. Denies SI. No trauma.

PMH: antisocial personality disorder; severe alcohol use disorder; cocaine use disorder; tobacco use (1 ppd x 7 yrs).
FH: father alcohol use disorder (incarcerations); mother MDD and GAD; brother OUD.

Exam: Vital signs within normal limits. Smells of alcohol; intoxicated but alert and redirectable. Otherwise unremarkable: pupils equal and reactive, no head trauma, heart and lungs normal, abdomen soft, moving all extremities.

Course: monitored in the ED, PO fluids, no medications required. Clinically sober and tolerating PO by morning.

Impression: acute alcohol intoxication in a patient with severe alcohol use disorder.
Disposition: discharged home with partner. Substance use treatment resources given. Follow up with PCP.

[Received by fax 08/07/2023]

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27M, seen two weeks after a minor car accident (9/17). He was the passenger; his friend was driving in the rain, lost traction and they slid into a barrier. He remembers the screech of the tires and the airbag going off. Walked away without a scratch and still has no pain anywhere. Did not seek care that night.

He allows that it was "pretty scary" in the moment but keeps coming back to the fact that nobody got hurt. Since then he's had his head down: he is on a construction job with a project deadline coming up and has been putting in overtime, and in whatever time is left he's studying for the state construction licensing exam. Asked how he's processing the accident, he says he'll deal with it when there's time and right now there are more important things to focus on. No intrusive memories or flashbacks, no nightmares, isn't avoiding cars or rides, not jumpy or on guard. Sleep short because of work and studying, not because of the accident. PHQ-9 3.

Prior ED visits Nov 2022 (police, legal) and Jul 2023 (intoxication), reviewed. Still smoking 1 ppd, drinking most nights though "less on work nights." Aspirin as before.

Exam: Vitals as charted. No bruising or seat-belt marks. Neck and spine nontender with full ROM. Chest wall and abdomen nontender. Neuro nonfocal.
Mental status: calm and cooperative, good eye contact, affect appropriate to content, speech normal. Thought process linear. No psychotic features, no signs of mania, mood described as "fine" and not depressed.

A/P
1. MVA as passenger, no injury. Normal exam. No imaging needed.
2. Stress around work deadlines and the licensing exam. He's coping by setting the accident aside, which seems to be working for now; no symptoms of acute stress disorder or PTSD. Occupational stress noted. Talked about sleep, and that alcohol will not help either the stress or the exam. Will reach out if anything about the accident starts to bother him.
3. Substance use: unchanged, brief counseling.
Flu shot at a nurse visit this month.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received 2026-03-19)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 01/30/2026, 10:25 to 15:40
Patient: Jacob Healey, 28 M. Allergies: NKDA.
Home meds: aspirin 325 mg daily, OTC.

CC: nausea, vomiting, blood in vomit.

HPI: 28 yo M with antisocial personality disorder and severe alcohol and cocaine use disorders, seen here before for intoxication and a legal matter. Began vomiting early this morning, multiple times; the last episode had a small amount of bright red blood mixed in. Was at a party last night, drank heavily and used drugs including cocaine. Has a bad headache going back several days and has been taking his aspirin regularly through it. No abdominal pain. No black or bloody stools.

Social: smokes 1 ppd (~10 yrs). Heavy daily alcohol with frequent binges. Cocaine.

Exam: Well-appearing, no distress. Hemodynamically stable, vitals per flowsheet. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no rebound, no guarding.

Labs: CBC normal, hemoglobin normal. PT/INR normal.

Course: no further hematemesis during 5 hours of observation; tolerated oral fluids.

Impression: stress-related mucosal disease (acute mucosal injury of the stomach) with small-volume hematemesis, in the setting of binge alcohol, cocaine and aspirin use. Low risk; outpatient management.

Plan: omeprazole 40 mg by mouth daily for 8 weeks (Rx sent). Stop aspirin and avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and naproxen. Stop alcohol and cocaine. Return for repeat or larger-volume bleeding, black stools, dizziness or fainting, or abdominal pain. Follow up with PCP within 1 week.

[Faxed 03/19/2026 at PCP office request]

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28M seen after ED visit 1/30. No ED paperwork with him and nothing sent to us; history is his.

Went to a party Thursday night, drank a lot and used cocaine. Woke up Friday morning vomiting, several times, and the last one had some bright red blood in it, "not a lot." He'd had a headache for a few days before and was taking his aspirin through it. ED did blood work which he was told was normal, watched him for a few hours, told him the stomach lining was irritated (he recalls "stress-related" something), started omeprazole 40 daily for 8 weeks and told him no aspirin. Since then: no further vomiting, no blood, no black stools, no abdominal pain, no lightheadedness. Taking the omeprazole every morning. Headache gone. Has not had aspirin since.

Drinking slowed a little this week, back to most nights; AUDIT-C 12. Smoking 1 ppd.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.

A/P
1. Hematemesis, small volume, ED dx stress-related mucosal disease with alcohol, cocaine and aspirin. Stable. Finish omeprazole 40 mg daily x 8 wks (ED Rx, on med list). Repeat CBC today. Requesting the ED record.
2. Aspirin: stopped, off his list for good.
3. Severe alcohol use disorder: this one got more traction than usual. Offered naltrexone, explained what it does and what it would mean with his drinking; also offered an addiction medicine referral. He thought about it and said no to both for now. Return precautions for bleeding reviewed.
4. Cocaine use disorder, nicotine dependence: counseled.
RTC after the omeprazole course, or sooner.
